chunks: And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

"When there are many sacrificial camels (budn), and you wish to mark them for sacrifice, the man enters between every two camels; he marks this one from the right side and that one from the left side. He does not mark them permanently until he is ready for Ihram. For indeed, when he marks and ties the neck-ring, Ihram becomes obligatory upon him, and it is in the status of Talbiyah."

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةِ: Talbiyah (the recitation of 'Here I am, O God')
key_terms.لِلْإِحْرَامِ: For Ihram (the sacred state of pilgrimage)

ai.seo_question: How should one mark sacrificial camels before entering the state of Ihram for Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal mechanism of *Ihram* for those bringing sacrificial animals (*Hadi*), establishing that the act of marking and equipping the camel serves as the formal declaration of intent, equivalent to the *Talbiyah*. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the camel as a proxy for the owner's ritual state, ensuring the sacrifice is properly consecrated before the Hajj rites commence. It underscores the practical application of *Ihram* boundaries, linking the physical preparation of the animal directly to the spiritual obligation of the pilgrim.
